phase_task.goal: Polyglot sandbox runners: implement Go, Rust, and TypeScript CLI runners that conform to the SAME sandbox contract as the Phase-3 Python reference runner, selectable via config (SANDBOX_RUNNER=python|go|rust|ts), and prove parity by running the SAME Phase-3 oracle suite against each. This is the "own and swap the core" evidence — one contract, multiple conforming implementations. Strictly additive: it must not touch or regress any core capability. The Python runner remains the default and the reference.

deliverables.d: For each of Go, Rust, TypeScript: a standalone CLI runner that implements the identical sandbox contract — receives (workspace snapshot + JSON patch envelope + resource limits), spins the locked-down container (--network=none, cpu/mem/disk, wall-clock kill, non-root, cap-drop, read-only rootfs + tmpfs, unique --name + explicit stop/rm on all exit paths — the Phase-5 leak fix must be replicated, not re-introduced), runs apply->build->test, and emits the SAME structured VerificationResult shape (applied/built/tests_passed/exit_code/stage/stdout_tail/stderr_tail/wall_clock_seconds/killed_reason). The result contract is the Phase-3 one, unchanged.

Config-driven selection: SANDBOX_RUNNER=python|go|rust|ts routes to the chosen runner via the existing build_sandbox_client factory / a runner-selection seam. No caller code changes to switch runners — only config. The control plane calls the same SandboxClient interface regardless.

Parity proof: the SAME Phase-3 oracle suite (good patch passes, bad patch surfaces real error text, network egress fails closed, wall-clock kill, host isolation, memory limit binds, zero container leak after timeout) runs against EACH runner and produces equivalent results. A parity test asserts the four runners agree on the same fixture inputs. Any runner that cannot be built/run in this environment is HONESTLY flagged (e.g. "Rust runner implemented + unit-tested; full Docker parity requires the toolchain image") rather than reported as passing untested.

Build integration: each runner builds via the Makefile/scripts (never inline docker), with its own build target and the cleanup trap. Toolchains live in their own build stages/images so `make up` (Python default) is unaffected and stays one-command.

The core is untouched: the agent loop, retrieval, index, journal, budget, API, and Python runner are not modified except for the minimal runner-selection seam. Run the full existing suite to prove zero regression.

phase_task.oracle: Via make (Docker + the respective toolchains): (1) each runner (go|rust|ts) passes the Phase-3 oracle set by its ACTUAL mechanism — good patch verified, bad patch returns REAL error text, egress fails closed, wall-clock kill reported, host isolation holds, memory limit binds, ZERO container leak after a timeout run (the Phase-5 fix replicated in each); (2) SANDBOX_RUNNER config switches the active runner with no caller code change — assert the same task verifies through each selected runner; (3) a parity test asserts all available runners return the equivalent VerificationResult for the same fixtures; (4) the full pre-existing suite still passes with the Python default — zero regression to any core capability; (5) `make up` still boots one-command keyless on the Python default, unaffected by the added toolchains; (6) any runner not fully Docker-parity-provable in this environment is explicitly flagged, not reported green. No proxies — a runner claimed "passing" must have run its oracle.
phase_task.docs: DESIGN.md / ADR-0003 (sandbox): extend with the multi-runner reality — one contract, four conforming implementations, config-selected — as the concrete "own and swap the core" evidence the assignment asks for. Document the parity results per runner and honestly flag any runner proven only at unit level vs full Docker parity. Update the "what we cut / would do next" if any runner is partial. Note that the Phase-5 container-leak fix is replicated in every runner (not just Python).
phase_task.stop: Do not start Phase 9 (dashboard). Report: for each of go/rust/ts — implemented? built in this env? which Phase-3 oracle clauses ran and passed by real mechanism vs flagged-unproven; the config-selection proof (same task through each runner); the parity-test result; confirmation of zero regression to the core (full suite green on Python default); and confirmation `make up` still boots one-command. Flag every runner that is implemented-but-not-fully-Docker-proven so it is not mistaken for verified.
